text:
Alex: Heads-up for the overnight crew — vendor X is running a large batch job that should hit our hosted tier around 01:00-03:00 UTC. Estimated 40–50% spike in token throughput for embeddings and gen routes. Please watch GPU pools and quota burn.
Meera: Thanks Alex — which pools are most likely to feel it? dedicated vs hosted autoscale?
Alex: Mostly hosted inference (shared-host-pool-1/2). Dedicated customers shouldn't be impacted but shared pools will absorb the burst. We have ~25% headroom now; if it creeps <15% we'll need to open burst or throttle lower-priority jobs.
OpsBot: [auto-snooze] Scheduled vendor batch window detected: vendor-x/batch-2026-03-18 01:00-03:00 UTC. Predicted QPS spike +48%. Linked report: https://monitoring.local/reports/vendor-x-2026-03-18
Jin: I can cover 00:45–03:30 UTC. I'll keep an eye on pool-util and be ready to toggle burst.
Rowan: If needed, use the emergency burst key `burst-enable shared-host-pool-1 --duration 20m` (ops-only). Also there's a soft quota `token-rate-limit` we can raise from 120k->160k for the window.
Casey: Embeddings quota:view shows customers A and B have large queued batches. If we enable burst, embeddings jobs will jump to hot nodes — watch memory pressure on g4dn/rtx pools.
Meera: Quick checklist for handoff: 1) confirm who is covering (Jin) 2) link to live graphs 3) thresholds for escalating to SRE (CPU%>80 && mem%>75 for >5m OR queue-delay>60s). Anyone object/add?
Alex: Sounds good. Live widgets: https://grafana.local/d/health/shared-pools and https://grafana.local/d/embeddings/queue-delay
Jin: Ack. I'll post updates every 30m and ping if headroom <15% or queue-delay >45s. Starting watch at 00:45 UTC.
Rowan: FYI I patched autoscaler smoothing earlier — it should prevent rapid oscillations. If you see a flapping scale event, hold changes for 10m and ping me before forced changes.
Casey: Can someone confirm whether customer B's batch has a retry loop? If yes, we may need to coordinate with support to stagger retries.
Alex: Support says customer B uses their own orchestrator with exponential backoff, but retries could still pile up if throughput tightens. I'll DM support to request a small delay window.
Meera: Jin — if you need more hands, @Rowan and I can rotate in at 02:30 UTC. Otherwise, we'll assume Jin owns the watch and do a normal handback at 03:35 UTC.
Jin: Good plan. I'll also run `kubectl top pods -n inference | grep shared-host` if things look odd and paste results.
OpsBot: [note] No current incidents. Alerting thresholds active for shared-host-pool-1: headroom<10%, scale-failures>1.
Alex: Thanks team. Leaving the thread open — please post brief check-ins. Final handoff note: Jin is on-call cover; escalate to eng-sre if autoscale fails or persistent OOMs appear.
Jin: First check-in 01:15 UTC — headroom 22%, queue-delay 12s, no action needed.
Meera: Thx. Next check-in 01:45 UTC from Jin then.
